He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Montgomery attended Lincoln Park Academy in [[Fort Pierce, Florida]] for middle school and started playing at the varsity level as a 6'8" seventh grader. As an eighth grader, Montgomery and the Greyhounds won the Florida District 12-4A championship.{{Cite web|url=http://www.tcpalm.com/news/st-lucie-county-notebook-seventh-grader-montgomery-turning-heads-at-lincoln-park-ep-381629477-342862592.html|title=St. Lucie County Notebook: Seventh-grader Montgomery turning heads at Lincoln Park|website=www.tcpalm.com|language=en|access-date=2019-02-13}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{Cite web|url=http://www.tcpalm.com/sports/high-school/basketball/2014-2015-district-12-4a-high-school-boys-basketball-preview--poll-ep-763834014-341335561.html|title=2014-2015 District 12-4A high school boys basketball preview {{!}} Poll|website=www.tcpalm.com|language=en|access-date=2019-02-13}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Montgomery first attended [[Montverde Academy]] for his freshmen and sophomore year, where he played alongside current Net [[Ben Simmons]]. He later transferred to [[Wheeler High School (Georgia)|Wheeler High School]] for his junior and senior year. He averaged 25.6 points, 13.6 rebounds, and 4.3 assists at Wheeler.{{cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6790|title=2018-19 Men's Basketball Roster : EJ Montgomery|website=Ukathletics.com|date=June 6, 2018 |access-date=January 2, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Montgomery originally committed to [[Auburn University]] on September 22, 2016. However, when Auburn was involved in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal|college basketball corruption scandal]], Montgomery decommitted on September 27, 2017.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/09/27/ej-montgomery-auburn-tigers-chuck-person-fbi-investigation|title=Auburn Loses Five-Star Recruit Amid FBI Investigation|website=Si.com|date=September 27, 2017 |access-date=January 2, 2019}} On April 9, 2018, Montgomery committed to play college basketball at the [[University of Kentucky]].{{cite web|url=http://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/index.ssf/2018/04/former_auburn_commit_ej_montgo.html|title=5-star former Auburn commit EJ Montgomery commits to Kentucky|website=Al.com|date=April 9, 2018 |access-date=January 2, 2019}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = E.J. Montgomery | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Fort Pierce, Florida|Fort Pierce, FL]] | highschool = [[Wheeler High School (Georgia)|Wheeler]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 215 | 40 = | commitdate = April 9, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Kentucky 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Kentucky Wildcats Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = kentucky | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 96 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 11 | 247 overall = 6 | espn overall = 14 | accessdate = June 4, 2018 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Montgomery had his first double-double of 11 points and 13 rebounds in a win over [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]]. As a freshman, Montgomery averaged 3.8 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=What the return of EJ Montgomery means for Kentucky |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/What-the-return-of-EJ-Montgomery-means-for-Kentucky-132445111/ |access-date=December 8, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=May 30, 2019}} On December 7, 2019, Montgomery scored a career-high 25 points as Kentucky defeated [[Fairleigh Dickinson Knights men's basketball|Fairleigh Dickinson]] 83–52.{{cite news |title=No. 8 Kentucky rolls Fairleigh Dickinson, 600th win at Rupp |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169879 |access-date=December 8, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 6, 2019}} In the regular season finale versus [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], Montgomery hit the game-winning tip-in with 11 seconds left. He averaged 6.1 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.1 blocks per game.{{cite news |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=Wildcats face difficult draft decisions |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Wildcats-face-difficult-draft-decisions-145154068 |access-date=March 18, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 18, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=EJ Montgomery completes Kentucky starters' exit for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29040029/ej-montgomery-completes-kentucky-starters-exit-nba-draft |access-date=April 15, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 15, 2020}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Montgomery signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=EJ Montgomery signs with Bucks |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Kentucky-basketball-EJ-Montgomery-free-agent-Milwaukee-Bucks-155019158/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=November 19, 2020}} He was waived on December 17. On January 4, 2021, he signed with [[BC Nevėžis|Nevėžis-OPTIBET]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/e-j-montgomery-signs-with-nevezis/|title=E.J. Montgomery signs with Nevezis|date=January 4, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 4, 2021 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }} On September 1, Montgomery signed with [[Soproni KC]] of the [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I/A (men's basketball)|Nemzeti Bajnokság I/A]].{{cite web |last1=Gabor |first1=Winter |title=E.J. Montgomery agreed terms with Sopron KC |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Hungary/news/702853/E.J.-Montgomery-agreed-terms-with-Sopron-KC |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 1, 2021 |date=September 1, 2021}} On August 3, 2022, Montgomery signed with [[Aomori Wat's]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].{{cite web|title=イー・ジェイ・モンゴメリー選手2022-23シーズン契約合意について|url=https://aomori-wats.jp/news/detail/id=16073|website=Aomori-Wats.jp|date=August 3, 2022|access-date=December 20, 2022|language=Japanese}} On October 28, 2024, Montgomery joined the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} On August 15, 2025, he
